guidelineReference: Resus Council UK Acute Coronary Syndromes 2021
title: Cardiac chest pain in the stadium toilets
setting: Stadium toilets. Elderly patient feeling unwell, pale, cold, clammy, complaining of severe indigestion/chest pain that won't go away.
verdictExplanation: Severe central chest pain, respiratory distress, and profound cardiogenic shock (BP 70/40, pulse 120 bpm). Sick: call 999 immediately and treat.

shared.circulation: Very weak pulse, skin is pale, cold, and clammy

history.history: Suffering from severe indigestion all day, became dizzy and collapsed/sat down in toilets
history.additional: Friend found him and called for first aid

followUp.question: What is your immediate priority action for this patient?

options.text: Call 999 immediately, sit him in the 'W' position, administer 300mg chewable aspirin, and monitor closely
Give him a glass of water and tell him to lie flat on the floor
Administer GTN spray repeatedly and tell him to walk to the exit
Give him an antacid tablet for his indigestion and leave him to rest

followUp.explanation: Suspected heart attack is a critical emergency. Call 999 immediately. Sit him in the 'W' position to ease breathing and cardiac strain. Administer 300mg chewable aspirin. Never lay flat (worsens breathing) or allow walking. Indigestion is a common mimic of myocardial infarction.

levelFlags.cfaNotes: Recognize cardiac symptoms, call 999. Place in W-position, administer aspirin 300mg chewable. Keep at rest.
levelFlags.erNotes: Suspected myocardial infarction with cardiogenic shock (BP 70/40). Give high-flow oxygen, give aspirin 300mg. Monitor vitals, prepare AED, and expedite ambulance.
